speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Can you tell me how old the child is and when you first noticed these skin lesions?

speaker: Patient
text: 2-year-old female. The patient's mother reports noticing multiple painless, nonpruritic papules on the child's abdomen. The child attends daycare where another child was reported to have similar lesions recently. Patient's brother had chickenpox one month ago. Immunizations are up-to-date.

speaker: Doctor
text: Are the papules flat-topped with a central indentation, and have you observed any lesions in different stages of development on her body? I would also like to know if she has had any fever or respiratory symptoms recently.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Skin-colored, nontender, pearly papules with central umbilication on the abdomen and extremities.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you, that description of pearly papules with central umbilication is highly characteristic. Given the daycare exposure and the appearance of the lesions, I am confident in my assessment. DIAGNOSIS READY: Molluscum contagiosum
